the number at the start of an edge is the step that traces it; a step nothing measures says so
You label an issue. The reader checks the label came before the last edit, then admits it as
a queue item.
The daemon runs its admission gates in a fixed order and claims one item only if every gate
allows it.
The planner attacks the spec for ambiguity and missing failure modes, halts on a blocker, and
otherwise writes the components and their acceptance criteria.
Each ready component gets its own working copy; nothing is measured yet.
The agent is told what the codebase looks like and what earlier components learned, before it
acts.
The agent works one story at a time and says when it is done. Only the stall detector and the
scope fence watch this loop; neither reads the code.
The checks that need no model run first: tests, types, lint, scope, the merge rules, the
tests' own quality, the approved fixtures.
A reviewer from another model family judges every acceptance criterion; a security reviewer
hunts vulnerabilities.
The findings, not the agent's summary, decide: pass, or write them into the next attempt's
context and retry.
What was learned about the artifact is written down while the diff is still the true delta.
The component is pushed, opened and merged; it is complete only when the merge is confirmed.
Integration tests run on the merged tiers; a failure is attributed to the last component
merged, which re-runs against the fresh base.
The run's outcome is folded into the ladder's evidence and appended to the journal.
